scores.claim_text: Arqit's first U.S. Department of War contract is in partnership with a large, leading U.S. IT vendor.

supports.edgar_fts_top_filers: Centricus (de-SPAC) and Arqit's own 20-Fs dominate; no IT-vendor counterparty disclosure surfaces in the top results.

scores.M_check: USAspending direct-recipient search + EDGAR full-text counterparty corroboration
scores.M_value: 0 federal contracts to Arqit as prime recipient; counterparty IT vendor unnamed in filing so cannot be CIK-restricted
scores.interpretation: Indirect prime-contract structure (sub through unnamed IT vendor) makes USAspending absence non-disqualifying, but the lack of NAMED counterparty plus zero direct federal-recipient record means the dollar magnitude is almost certainly small. FY25 revenue of $530K corroborates that this contract is sub-scale relative to the headline framing. Calibration heuristic 3 (planned vs operational): scoped between 'has revenue' and 'commercial deployment' — small but real. Heuristic 7 (counterparty-disclosure threshold) is partly inapplicable because the U.S. IT vendor is unnamed, so we cannot CIK-restrict; but the marketing-heavy framing of a $530K-revenue company calling itself the holder of a 'first U.S. Department of War contract' is a vagueness signal.

scores.claim_text: Arqit's largest license contract is a multi-year agreement via a Middle East IT vendor partner to several government agencies of a major Middle Eastern country.

supports.edgar_fts_SKA-Platform_filers: Only Arqit's own 2024 and 2025 20-Fs reference SKA-Platform; no third-party filer corroborates.
supports.edgar_fts_non_Arqit_filers: Only Centricus (the de-SPAC vehicle) mentions Arqit; no Middle East IT-vendor counterparty (e.g. e&, STC, Mobily, Etisalat) surfaces.

scores.M_check: EDGAR full-text product-name (SKA-Platform) and company-name corroboration across all filers
scores.M_value: Two SKA-Platform mentions, both self-disclosure; zero independent counterparty filings
scores.interpretation: The Middle East end customer and IT vendor partner are both unnamed, so EDGAR cannot CIK-restrict; and a Middle Eastern government's IT vendor often is not an SEC filer. Heuristic 7 caveats apply (non-US counterparty disclosure threshold weaker). However, the FY25 revenue table shows one customer at >56% of $530K (~$297K), meaning this 'largest license contract' is sub-$300K of recognized revenue — a stark scale mismatch with the qualitative framing ('largest license contract, multi-year, several government agencies'). Heuristic 11 (revenue-recognition pattern) and Heuristic 3 (planned vs operational) both apply: contract may be signed but GAAP revenue is tiny. MODERATE rather than SEVERE because non-US end customer reduces M-source visibility.

scores.claim_text: NetworkSecure integrates with OEM firewalls, routers and edge platforms from Juniper, Fortinet, and Cisco.

supports.edgar_fts_NetworkSecure_filers: Arqit's own 20-Fs plus unrelated Allot Ltd (different product); no Cisco/Juniper/Fortinet filings mention Arqit or NetworkSecure

scores.M_check: EDGAR full-text counterparty corroboration restricted to Cisco / Juniper / Fortinet CIKs
scores.M_value: Zero counterparty disclosure; 'NetworkSecure' is a generic product name not uniquely tied to Arqit in EDGAR
scores.interpretation: Claim language is carefully scoped ('available to integrate with' — not 'commercially deployed by' or 'design-win at'). Under Heuristic 4 and Heuristic 7, technical-compatibility / 'integrates with' language is the weakest tier of partnership claim and does not require counterparty disclosure (the OEMs would not list every third-party VPN tool). However, the absence of even a press-release or partner-page mention surfaced via EDGAR, combined with FY25 revenue of $530K and one customer being 56% of that, suggests no meaningful commercial pipeline through Juniper/Fortinet/Cisco. Score MODERATE — claim is technically defensible (integration is plausible / cheap) but the implied 'OEM channel' is not yet producing revenue.

scores.claim_text: 28 granted patents and 17 pending patents in the UK, plus issued patents in U.S., EU, Singapore, Japan, Korea and Canada.

sample_granted_titles: OPTICAL SWITCHING FOR QUANTUM KEY DISTRIBUTION (2026-04-28)
RANDOM NUMBER GENERATION IN QUANTUM KEY DISTRIBUTION (2026-02-24)
A SYSTEM AND METHOD FOR TIME SYNCHRONISATION (2026-03-10)
A SYSTEM AND METHOD FOR BEAM ALIGNMENT (2025-11-18)
KEY EXCHANGE PROTOCOL FOR SATELLITE BASED QUANTUM NETWORK

scores.M_check: USPTO Open Data Portal assignee search with quantum/key/encryption category bucket
scores.M_value: 17 US-granted patents, 30 US applications total; 21 of 30 categorize into 'quantum_safe' bucket
scores.interpretation: Heuristic 8 PASS threshold (>=10 granted with claimed-technology-area hit) met. US grants alone (17) plus the company's separately disclosed 28 UK grants is plausible for a 7-year-old QKD/PQC company. Titles are squarely on-thesis (QKD, key exchange, optical switching) — not a Nikola pattern. Note that several granted patents relate to SATELLITE-based QKD, which is the discontinued satellite division — IP value may be impaired for the going-forward (terrestrial SKA) thesis, but the headline patent count is corroborated.

scores.claim_text: Total revenue FY2025 was $530K (FY24: $293K; FY23: $640K); one customer represented >56% of FY25 revenue.
scores.M_check: Intrinsic to filing: Note 2 Revenue + Note 23 Retained earnings (cohort heuristics 10 and 11)
scores.M_value: Cumulative retained-earnings deficit $373.8M against TTM revenue of $530K; revenue actually FELL from $640K (FY23) to $293K (FY24) and only partially recovered. Largest 'multi-year' contract is one customer at $297K.
scores.interpretation: Heuristic 11 (revenue-recognition pattern): the qualitative claims about 'first U.S. Department of War contract', 'largest license contract' to a Middle East government, OEM channels with Juniper/Fortinet/Cisco, and major partner programs (Oracle Defense Ecosystem, Vodafone Tomorrow Street) are RADICALLY out of proportion to GAAP revenue. After 4+ post-deSPAC years, a quantum-encryption software company with $530K total revenue is functionally pre-commercial. Combined with the going-concern-adjacent cash position (12 months of runway only because of the just-completed $37M ATM raise into a ~$36M cash balance with $30M annual burn — and only if no further ATM dilution materially impairs equity value), this is a hard signal that the customer-pipeline framing is marketing relative to operational reality.

scores.claim_text: Selected as member of Oracle Defense Ecosystem (June 2025); joined Vodafone's Tomorrow Street Scaleup X 2025 cohort (August 2025).
scores.M_check: EDGAR full-text counterparty corroboration at Oracle and Vodafone CIKs + global Oracle Defense Ecosystem phrase
scores.M_value: Zero mention of Arqit in either Oracle's or Vodafone's filings; Oracle Defense Ecosystem itself surfaces only once globally — not in Oracle's own 10-K.
scores.interpretation: Heuristic 4 (investment vs operating) and Heuristic 7 lower bound: 'membership in an ecosystem' and 'innovation-center cohort' are partner-program marketing relationships, not commercial design wins. The fact that neither Oracle nor Vodafone reference Arqit in any SEC filing is consistent with the program being non-material to those counterparties — i.e., real but small. Score MODERATE rather than RED because Arqit accurately characterized these as 'collaborations' rather than customer contracts; the underdelivery is in the implied uplift to commercialization.

scores.claim_text: Prior-period restatement of FY24/FY23 for IFRS 2 share-based-payment error; prior FY22 material weaknesses; 25-for-1 reverse share split (Sep 2024); $7.0M class-action settlement provision (Oct 2025 term sheet).
scores.M_check: Intrinsic to filing: Note 21 Prior period error, Risk Factors (material weakness), Definitions (Reverse Share Split), Note 25 Provisions
scores.M_value: Three distinct distress fingerprints stacked: (1) second restatement in this company's short public life (the 2022 financials were also restated; this 2025 filing now restates FY23 and FY24 for IFRS 2), (2) 25-for-1 reverse split — extreme ratio, characteristic of names that have lost 95%+ of de-SPAC valuation, (3) actual cash class-action settlement ($7M = ~19% of cash on hand, ~13x annual revenue).
scores.interpretation: Heuristic 10 (delisting / going-concern fingerprints) explicitly elevates these as claim-adjacent signals. The 25:1 reverse split alone implies the pre-split price was a small fraction of the $1 Nasdaq minimum-bid threshold. The repeated restatement pattern (FY21/FY22 originally; now FY23/FY24) plus prior material weaknesses indicates persistent internal-control issues. The class-action provision being recorded simultaneously with a 'first U.S. Department of War contract' announcement is the kind of mixed-signal disclosure that historically precedes further dilution / equity events. RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE on the basis of stacked distress markers.

scores.claim_text: Raised ~$37.18M via ATM Program in FY25 (1,959,420 shares); cash $36.978M at 9/30/25 vs $29.553M operating burn; net loss $35.343M.
scores.M_check: Intrinsic: 5.B Liquidity, Cash Flow Summary, Note 22 Share capital
scores.M_value: ATM raises now cover ~125% of annual operating burn; without them, cash runway would be ~12 months from a $36.98M base, but ATM dilution this year was ~13% of post-split share count (1.96M / 15.29M). Reported retained-earnings deficit is $373.8M — nearly 5x current cash. Going-concern language was specifically rebutted by management.
scores.interpretation: Heuristics 10 and 11: a quantum-encryption software business that requires continuous ATM equity issuance to cover operating burn, with revenue still under $1M after five years public, is in structural distress regardless of management's going-concern reassurance. The auditor accepted the going-concern basis only on the back of management's 'ability to raise additional funding' — i.e., further ATM dilution. SEVERE rather than RED because the auditor signed off and the cash position is technically adequate for 12+ months; but the dilution math (issuing 1.96M shares of a 13.3M share base just to keep the lights on) is itself a strong signal that the equity structure is in a continuous downward spiral.
